title: Ramadan: the last ten, fully
tomorrow: after a month of fasting, is a party really worship?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ramadan as the book's month: Jibril and the Prophet going over it, night after night. The book in the month. Now the month's final stretch, and a night with no date.
screen: `THE BOOK IN THE MONTH.` → `A NIGHT WITH NO DATE.`

segments.voice: Some flyers refuse to print a date. One night this month, they say, and the people who care start showing up every night. The Qur'an has a night like that. It calls it the Night of Power, and says, in Pickthall's words, "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months." Then it never says which night. Stranger still, a hadith says the Prophet ﷺ once came out to tell people the date. And didn't.
screen: `ONE NIGHT THIS MONTH. WHICH?` → `BETTER THAN A THOUSAND MONTHS.` → `HE CAME OUT TO TELL THEM.`

segments.voice: Here's the report, from Sahih al-Bukhari. He came out to tell them the night, and found two men quarreling. And the knowledge of it was taken up. Then he said: perhaps that is better for you. Seek it in the odd nights of the last ten. So an argument between two people cost everyone the date, and the loss turned into something else. Instead of one night circled on a calendar, ten nights of searching, the odd ones especially. That's the puzzle solved: the night is hidden so the whole stretch gets lived. And the Prophet lived it. 'A'isha describes the last ten: he tightened his waist-wrap, gave the nights life with prayer, and woke his family. He also stayed in the masjid in those days, in i'tikaf, a retreat, setting ordinary life aside to pray. That's what fully means here. Not one big night guessed right. Ten nights, given over, with the household woken up to share them. Some companions held the night was a particular one; the hadith keeps the door open on all the odd nights. One to tell a friend tonight: the date of the Night of Power was lost because two people argued.
screen: `TWO MEN QUARRELING.` · `PERHAPS THAT IS BETTER FOR YOU.` · `HE WOKE HIS FAMILY.` · `I'TIKAF: A RETREAT.` · then, large: `THE LAST TEN.`

segments.voice: Take the next ten nights you have, or the last ten of the next Ramadan, and mark the odd ones. For each, choose one small thing you'd give that night: a page, a prayer, a few quiet minutes before sleep. Then sit with the list in front of you for the rest of the time.
screen: `MARK THE ODD NIGHTS.` · `ONE SMALL THING FOR EACH.`

segments.voice: Ramadan: the month of fasting. Its last ten nights are its final stretch, and the Night of Power is hidden among the odd ones.
Hold on to this: the last ten, given fully, because any odd night could be the one. The search is the gift.

fork.setup: your friend works early shifts and can stay up late on only two of the last ten nights. which two?
options: just the one night everyone says is it; the rest don't matter.
two of the odd nights, and something small on the others.

fork.reveal: the hadith says seek it in the odd nights of the last ten. no date is fixed, so the search is spread out, and the small things on the other nights count too.

chat.says: Dadi drew stars on five nights of the last ten on her calendar. why those? why not one big night?
options: Those are the odd nights. The date was hidden, so the search is spread across them.

chat.meaning: The Prophet came out to tell the date, but it was taken up; he said seek it in the odd nights of the last ten.

Night of Power.meaning: Laylat al-Qadr, the hidden night in Ramadan's last ten

i'tikaf.meaning: a retreat: staying in the masjid to pray

'A'isha.meaning: a wife of the Prophet who reported much of his home life

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of reports of the Prophet's words and deeds
